conviction_note: ServiceTitan lost 16.8% in the five sessions into the print with no filing since 17 August and no company-specific cause anywhere in the capture, while two institutions newly crossed 5% in late July and early August; that says the air pocket is sector and rates rather than the quarter, which is a mild positive, but the capture ran zero search queries so I cannot rule out a cause I simply cannot see - hence a number well inside the 6.94% median.

findings.finding: Two initial Schedule 13G filings - new holders crossing 5%, not amendments - were accepted eight days apart on 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-06, alongside 13G/As on 07-21 and 08-13, and there is no Schedule 13D anywhere in the 400-day lookback and no S-1, S-3 or 424B of any kind; so two institutions were building 5%-plus positions while the stock traded in the $90s, and no registered supply was created to meet them.
findings.corpus_ref: filings.json, CIK 0001638826: SCHEDULE 13G filing_date 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-06, SCHEDULE 13G/A 2026-07-21 and 2026-08-13; no 13D and no registration statement other than S-8s (2025-10-21, 2026-03-25)
findings.why_not_priced: 13G initial filings are the least-watched ownership event there is - they arrive without a press release, they are not in any earnings preview, and this capture's news channel ran zero queries on all eleven sweeps so nothing connected them to the print. If they were priced, the stock would not have fallen from $98.04 on 08-31 to $81.58 on 09-08, a 16.8% five-session air pocket that no filing (the last was a Form 4 accepted 2026-08-17) and no captured item explains, with the only contemporaneous commentary in the corpus attributing it to macro - 'headed to 80 or lower if there is a rate hike', 2026-09-04.
findings.independence: Weakly corroborated from a different source: the StockTwits digest records every published price target in the run-in - Cowen $125, Morgan Stanley $124, Piper $115, BTIG and Truist $110, BMO $103, Baird $94 on 2026-06-10, then Freedom $155, KeyBanc $125, Needham $125, Morgan Stanley $115 on 2026-07-03, with a consensus target given as $104 on 2026-06-12 - so the entire published range sits above the $81.58 spot and the lowest of them is 15% above it, meaning the sell side had not marked its numbers down with the price. Those targets are two to three months stale and price targets lag, which is why this is a support rather than a second finding.

findings.finding: Insider disposition filings ran essentially weekly from mid-June to mid-August - roughly twenty Form 4s (06/17 x4, 06/18 x6, 06/24 x2, 06/25, 06/30, 07/02, 07/07, 07/08 x2, 07/10, 07/14, 07/15 x3, 07/16 x2, 07/20, 08/05, 08/13, 08/17) and fourteen Form 144 sale notices (06/23, 07/01 x3, 07/07, 07/09 x3, 07/15, 07/16 x3, 08/04, 08/11, 08/12, 08/14) - and then stopped completely after 2026-08-17, three weeks before the print; that is persistent post-IPO overhead supply which is mechanically absent during the pre-release blackout and returns once the window reopens.
findings.corpus_ref: filings.json, CIK 0001638826, Form 4 and Form 144 entries 2026-06-17 through 2026-08-17, and the absence of any filing between 2026-08-17 and the 2026-09-08 print
findings.why_not_priced: Individual Form 4s are the most-aggregated filing there is, so I am claiming very little here - only that the cadence, and the fact that this is a December 2024 IPO still working through lockup-expiry distribution, is the structural reason the stock failed at $100 three times (the digest calls it a 'triple top' on 2026-07-22, a 'quadruple top' on 2026-07-28, then $100.64 on 08-27 before a full retrace). It is signed negative because it caps the upside on my first finding rather than adding to it.
findings.independence: Deliberately points the opposite way to finding 1 and shares the same file, filings.json, so the two must be collapsed to one source cluster; I am keeping both because the honest state of this name is that supply and accumulation are both visible in the same index and I cannot rank them. none.
